findings.summary: The edge from Start to Process has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows 'Start' box bottom '└────┬────┘' followed by five entirely blank rows before the 'Process' box starts — no '│' or arrowhead at all. Compare the Process→End edge immediately below, which renders '│' on four rows then a '▼' arrowhead. The SVG's path id="...-L_A_B_0" (Start→Process) exists with marker-end, so the connector should be present.

findings.summary: The edge from Start to the 'Is it sunny?' decision node has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows Start's bottom border '╰───────┬──────╯' followed by five blank rows before the diamond '◇──────────────◇' starts — no '│' or arrowhead. Every other edge in this diagram (the Yes/No branches into 'Go to the park'/'Stay indoors', and the merge into 'Finish') renders a visible '▼' arrowhead. The SVG's path id="...-L_A_B_0" (Start→B) exists with marker-end, so this connector should be present too.

findings.summary: The edge from React App to State Manager (inside the Frontend subgraph) has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows React App's bottom border '└───────┬───────┘' followed by five blank rows (just the outer cluster border '│ │') before the State Manager box starts — no '│' or arrowhead. By contrast, the State Manager→API Server and API Server→Database edges both render a continuous '│' column ending in '▼'. The SVG's path id="...-L_A_B_0" (React App→State Manager) exists with marker-end, so the connector should be present.

findings.summary: The edge from Load Balancer to the US West Region's Web Server has an incomplete connector where it enters the cluster.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows the left-hand vertical line reaching the cluster border row ('│ │           US West Region │ │') and then going blank for the next two rows, with the West Web Server box starting with no incoming arrow. In the same two rows, the parallel Load Balancer→US East Web Server edge shows a continuous '│' then '▼' reaching its Web Server box. The SVG's path id="...-L_E_C_0" (Load Balancer→C, the US West Web Server) exists with marker-end ending near the node, so the West connector should reach the node the same way the East one does.

findings.summary: The edge from main to develop has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII row '│ main ├     │ develop ├─────►│ feature/auth ├─────────►│ PR Review │' shows main's right border as an open stub '├' followed by blank space (no dashes or arrowhead) before reaching develop, while the develop→feature/auth and feature/auth→PR Review edges on the same row both render a full '─────►' connector. The SVG's path id="...-L_A_B_0" (main→develop) exists with marker-end, so a connector should be drawn here too.

findings.summary: The edge from the initial pseudostate to 'Idle' has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows the start-state circle '●──────────────────●' followed by five entirely blank rows before the 'Idle' box starts — no '│' or arrowhead. By contrast, the Done→[end] edge at the bottom of the same diagram renders four '│' rows then a '▼' arrowhead into the end-state box. The SVG's path id="...-edge0" ([*]→Idle) exists with marker-end, so a connector should be present here too.

findings.summary: The edge from the initial pseudostate to 'Closed' has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows the start-state circle '●────────────────────●' followed by five entirely blank rows before the 'Closed' box starts — no '│' or arrowhead, whereas every transition further down (connect, success, timeout, close, error, done, max_retries, and Closed→[end]) renders a visible connector with an arrowhead or '◄'. The SVG's path id="...-edge0" ([*]→Closed) exists with marker-end, so a connector should be present here too.

findings.summary: The 'Hello Bob!' message (Alice to Bob) has no arrowhead in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII renders the first message as '│────────────────' with no terminating arrow, while the second message ('Hi Alice!', Bob to Alice) renders '◀╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧╧' with a leading '◀' arrowhead of the same length. The SVG's messageLine0 (data-from="Alice" data-to="Bob") has marker-end="url(#...-arrowhead)", so the first message should end in an arrowhead at Bob's lifeline just like the second one does.

findings.summary: The 'Login' message (Client to Server) has no arrowhead in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII renders the Login message as '│──────────────────────── ' with no terminating arrow into Server's lifeline, while all three alt-branch replies (200 OK, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden) render a leading '◀' arrowhead into Client. The SVG's messageLine0 (data-from="C" data-to="S") has marker-end="url(#...-arrowhead)", so the Login message should end in an arrowhead at Server's lifeline the same way the replies do.

findings.summary: The 'Click Login' message (User to Client App) has no arrowhead in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII renders the first message as '│─────────────────── ' with no terminating arrow into Client App's lifeline, while every other message in this flow (Authorization request, Login page, Credentials, Authorization code, Exchange code for token, Access token, Request + token, Protected resource, Display data) renders a visible '▶', '◀', or '╧'-dashed arrowhead at its destination. The SVG's messageLine0 (data-from="U" data-to="App") has marker-end="url(#...-arrowhead)", so the first message should end in an arrowhead at Client App's lifeline the same way the rest do.

findings.summary: The association edge from EventEmitter to Observer has no connector line in the ASCII output.
findings.evidence: ASCII shows EventEmitter's closing border '└────────────────────────────┘' followed by three entirely blank rows before the Observer box starts — no '│' or arrowhead, unlike the two realization edges elsewhere in the same diagram (Subject←EventEmitter and Observer←Logger/Alerter), which all render a '△' triangle and a dashed '┊' line connecting the classes. The SVG's path id="...-id_EventEmitter_Observer_4" (EventEmitter→Observer) exists with marker-end="url(#...-dependencyEnd)", so a connector should be drawn here too.
